'''David Wesley Climer'''<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.legistorm.com/person/bio/26438/David_Wesley_Climer.html |title=South Carolina State Sen. Wes Climer |publisher=LegiStorm}}</ref> (born September 26, 1982) is an [[American people|American]] politician. Since 2016, Climer has represented the 15th District ([[York County, South Carolina|York]]) in the [[South Carolina Senate]]. He is a member of the [[South Carolina Republican Party|Republican Party]].<ref>{{cite web |title=The Voter's Self Defense System |url=https://justfacts.votesmart.org/candidate/biography/168929/wes-climer |website=Vote Smart |accessdate=June 3, 2020}}</ref> He resigned from the state senate, effective November 3, 2026.<ref>https://scdailygazette.com/2026/06/22/gop-senator-running-for-congress-resigns-enabling-voters-to-replace-him-in-november/</ref>

== Political career ==

=== Congressional aide ===
From 2006 to 2011, Climer worked as a Washington, DC-based [[Congressional aide]] for Republicans US Rep. [[Patrick McHenry]], US Senator [[Elizabeth Dole]], and Senator [[Bill Cassidy]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Holdman |first=Jessica |date=2025-07-31 |title=Rock Hill state senator launches bid for SC's 5th Congressional District • SC Daily Gazette |url=https://scdailygazette.com/2025/07/31/rock-hill-state-senator-launches-bid-for-scs-5th-congressional-district/ |access-date=2025-08-04 |website=SC Daily Gazette |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== South Carolina Senate ===
Climer has represented South Carolina's 15th Senate District since 2016, when he defeated Republican [[Robert W. Hayes Jr.]] in the Republican primary. Before that, Hayes had represented the district since 1991.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Marchant |first=Bristow |date=June 18, 2016 |title=A closer look at how Climer unseated SC Sen. Hayes |url=https://www.thestate.com/news/politics-government/politics-columns-blogs/the-buzz/article84640827.html |access-date=April 21, 2024 |work=The State}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=South Carolina Legislature Online - Member Biography |url=https://www.scstatehouse.gov/member.php?code=0356818139 |accessdate=June 3, 2020 |website=www.scstatehouse.gov}}</ref>

In the primary race, Climer was endorsed by Governor [[Nikki Haley]], and supported by the [[Club for Growth]] and a PAC affiliated with Haley, Great Day SC PAC.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Marchant |first=Bristow |date=June 18, 2016 |title=A closer look at how Climer unseated SC Sen. Hayes |url=https://www.thestate.com/news/politics-government/politics-columns-blogs/the-buzz/article84640827.html |access-date=August 4, 2025 |work=The State Newspaper}}</ref>

Climer chairs the Senate Agriculture and Natural Resources Committee, and serves on the Senate Family and Veterans' Services, Finance, Labor Commerce and Industry, Legislative Oversight and Transportation Committees.<ref>{{Cite web |title=South Carolina Legislature Online - Committee |url=https://www.scstatehouse.gov/committee.php?chamber=S |access-date=2025-08-04 |website=www.scstatehouse.gov}}</ref>

==== Legislative lawsuit ====
On June 9, 2025, Climer and his attorney, former South Carolina Senator [[Dick Harpootlian]], sued the State of South Carolina over their vote in the 2025 state budget to give themselves pay raises, which they stated is in violation of the State constitution. Climer declined the additional money, as did 2 other members of the Senate and 34 members of the South Carolina House of Representatives.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-09 |title=SC senator sues to stop in-district pay raise for lawmakers |url=https://www.southcarolinapublicradio.org/sc-news/2025-06-09/sc-senator-sues-to-stop-in-district-pay-raise-for-lawmakers |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=South Carolina Public Radio |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2025-06-09 |title=SC senator details legal challenge opposing pay raises for state lawmakers |url=https://www.wistv.com/2025/06/09/sc-senator-files-legal-challenge-opposing-pay-raises-state-lawmakers/ |access-date=2025-06-09 |website=WIS-TV |language=en}}</ref>

=== 2026 congressional race ===
{{Main|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in South Carolina}}

On July 31, 2025, Climer announced his bid for the [[South Carolina's congressional districts|South Carolina Congressional District 5]] US House Seat.  Incumbent [[Ralph Norman]] had announced his intention to run in the [[2026 South Carolina gubernatorial election]]. Climer endorsed Norman in that race.<ref>{{Cite news |last=O'Neill |first=Nora |date=August 1, 2025 |title=SC senator announces run for Ralph Norman's 5th District seat in Congress |url=https://www.heraldonline.com/news/politics-government/article311540366.html |access-date=August 4, 2025 |work=The Herald}}</ref>

On August 21, 2025, Norman announced his endorsement of Climer as his successor in Congress.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2025-08-21 |title=US Rep. Ralph Norman endorses SC state Sen. Wes Climer to succeed him in Congress |url=https://www.wistv.com/2025/08/21/us-rep-ralph-norman-endorses-sc-state-sen-wes-climer-succeed-him-congress/ |access-date=2025-08-24 |website=WIS-TV |language=en}}</ref>

On February 7, 2026, Climer announced that he would resign in November 2026, concurrent with the passage of a joint resolution by the General Assembly allowing replacement elections for legislators submitting irrevocable resignations by March 1 to take place during the June Primaries, rather than in separate special elections.
